items.prompt:
A student is telling the class about her hamster. She says: 'My hamster Pepper is golden with a white patch on his nose and tiny dark eyes.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is better?
  A) A photograph of Pepper showing his golden fur and white nose patch.
  B) A photograph of a bag of hamster food.

Write A or B.

steps: The description is about what Pepper looks like.
Option A shows Pepper's actual appearance, matching the description.
Option B shows hamster food, which is not connected to what Pepper looks like.
A visual should show what the description is about.

items.prompt:
A student is telling the class how to make a paper chain for decoration. He says: 'Cut strips of paper. Loop one strip into a circle and tape it. Then loop the next strip through the first circle and tape it. Keep going until you have a long chain.'

He wants to add a visual. Which is better?
  A) A photograph of a decorated classroom.
  B) A step-by-step drawing showing: a flat strip, a strip looped into a circle, a second strip linked through the first.

Write A or B.

steps: The student is explaining steps in a process: how to link paper strips.
Option B (step-by-step drawing) shows each stage of the process as described.
Option A (decorated classroom) shows a final result but not the process of making it.
When describing a process, a step-by-step diagram is the best visual.

items.prompt:
A student is describing where she lives. She says: 'I live three blocks north of school. If you walk past the park on the corner and then turn left at the red mailbox, you will reach my house.'

She wants to add a visual. Which is better?
  A) A simple hand-drawn map showing the school, the park, the red mailbox, and her house.
  B) A photograph of the inside of her bedroom.

Write A or B.

steps: The student is giving directions: a route from school to her house.
Option A (map) shows the route with the landmarks she described.
Option B (bedroom photo) shows part of her home but not the route or landmarks.
When a description involves directions and locations, a map is the best visual.

items.prompt:
A student is describing the water cycle. He says: 'Water evaporates from oceans and lakes, rises as vapor, cools into clouds, falls as rain or snow, and flows back to the ocean.'

He has two visual options:
  Option A: A labeled diagram of the full water cycle as a loop, with arrows showing each stage.
  Option B: A photograph of rain falling.

Both are related to the topic. Which is better for this specific description and why?
items.answer: Option A is better. The student is describing a cycle with multiple stages that repeat in a loop. The diagram with arrows shows all the stages and makes the circular nature of the cycle visible. A photograph of rain falling shows only one stage (precipitation) and misses the rest of the process. When describing a multi-step cycle, a diagram is more helpful than a single photograph.

steps: The description covers five stages in a repeating cycle.
Option A (loop diagram with arrows) shows all five stages and the circular nature.
Option B (rain photo) shows only one stage.
A cycle diagram is the right visual for a description about a process that repeats.
Option A supports the full description; Option B supports only one part of it.

items.prompt:
A student is describing a book about a girl who moves from one city to another. She says: 'The main character, Zara, wears bright orange sneakers, keeps her hair in two puffs, and always carries a worn leather notebook.'

She has two visual options:
  Option A: A photograph of a city street.
  Option B: A drawing of Zara with orange sneakers, two puffs in her hair, and a worn notebook in her hand.

Both are related to the book. Which is better for this specific description and why?
items.answer: Option B is better. The student is describing what the character looks like. A drawing of Zara with the specific features described — orange sneakers, two puffs, worn notebook — shows the listener exactly what she described. A city street photograph shows a setting from the book, but it does not show Zara at all. A visual should match the specific content of the description, not just the general topic.

steps: The description is about Zara's appearance: sneakers, hair, notebook.
Option B (drawing of Zara) shows all three described features.
Option A (city street) shows a setting but not the character being described.
When a description is about a person's appearance, an illustration of that person is the right visual.
Option B directly supports the description; Option A does not.

items.prompt:
A student is describing a survey she did in her class. She says: 'I asked how everyone gets to school. Twelve students take the bus, six walk, four ride a bike, and three are dropped off.'

She has two visual options:
  Option A: A photograph of a school bus.
  Option B: A bar chart showing four categories (bus, walk, bike, drop-off) with the correct numbers.

Both are related to the survey. Which is better for this description and why?
items.answer: Option B is better. The student is presenting data — specific numbers for four different categories. A bar chart shows all four numbers clearly and lets listeners compare them. A photograph of a school bus shows only one category (the bus) and none of the other numbers. When a description includes multiple numbers and comparisons, a chart is the best visual.

steps: The description presents four numbers across four categories.
Option B (bar chart) shows all four numbers and allows comparison.
Option A (bus photo) shows one category only and no numbers.
A bar chart is the right visual for presenting survey data.
Option B supports the full description; Option A supports only one detail.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph:

'My neighborhood is shaped like a big rectangle. The north side is a busy road with stores. The south side is quiet and mostly houses. A park runs along the east edge, and a railroad track runs along the west edge. My street runs right through the middle from east to west.'

What type of visual would best support this description? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a simple top-down map of the neighborhood rectangle. The north edge should be labeled 'busy road with stores,' the south edge 'quiet houses,' the east edge 'park,' and the west edge 'railroad track.' A line through the middle labeled 'my street' should run from east to west. This visual makes the spatial layout clear in a single glance — something that would take many sentences to describe in words.

steps: The paragraph describes a spatial layout: a rectangle with specific features on each side.
A top-down map is the ideal visual for any spatial description.
The map should show: north = stores, south = houses, east = park, west = railroad, center = street.
Labels connect the visual directly to the words in the description.
A photograph of any one feature would not show the whole neighborhood layout.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about her family:

'My family is big. My great-grandma Rosa is at the top. She had two children: my grandma Lucia and my great-uncle Benito. Grandma Lucia had my mom and my aunt Pilar. My mom had me and my little brother.'

What type of visual would best support this description? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a family tree diagram with five levels. At the top: Great-grandma Rosa. Below her, two branches: Grandma Lucia and Great-uncle Benito. Below Grandma Lucia: Mom and Aunt Pilar. Below Mom: the student and her little brother. Each person should be in a labeled box with lines connecting parents to children. This makes the family relationships visual and easy to follow.

steps: The paragraph describes a family across four generations.
A family tree diagram is the standard and most effective visual for family relationships.
Level 1: Great-grandma Rosa. Level 2: Grandma Lucia and Great-uncle Benito. Level 3: Mom and Aunt Pilar. Level 4: the student and her brother.
Lines connecting boxes show parent-child relationships.
A photograph of the family would show faces but not the generational structure and relationships described.
